C08-M06-L02-F1.title: The Admiralty grading system: two independent axes
C08-M06-L02-F1.caption: Source reliability (A-F) and information credibility (1-6) are judged separately and combined into a grade such as B2.
C08-M06-L02-F1.alt: Table with four columns: Code, Source reliability, Code, Information credibility. Six rows: A Completely reliable and 1 Confirmed by other sources; B Usually reliable and 2 Probably true; C Fairly reliable and 3 Possibly true; D Not usually reliable and 4 Doubtful; E Unreliable and 5 Improbable; F Reliability cannot be judged and 6 Truth cannot be judged. Row tones run green, blue, violet, orange, red, slate. Note: pick one value from each side independently; F and 6 mean cannot be judged, not bad.
C08-M06-L02-F1.note: Pick one value from each side independently (for example B2 or F1); F and 6 mean 'cannot be judged', not 'bad'.

C08-M06-L02-F2.title: From received indicator to permitted action
C08-M06-L02-F2.caption: How producer confidence, separate source and information grades, local corroboration and ageing combine into a score that decides block, alert or context only.
C08-M06-L02-F2.alt: Flow of six steps, top to bottom. Receive indicator: producer confidence, e.g. conf= 60. Grade source: reliability A-F. Grade information: credibility 1-6. Corroborate locally: own sightings and detections, trace origins. Apply age: valid_until or decay. Action by threshold: 80+ block where safe, 50-79 alert, under 50 context only. A dashed loop labelled new sighting or report: re-grade and reset age runs from the last step back to Grade information.

steps.label: Corroborate locally
steps.sub: own sightings and detections; trace origins

steps.label: Action by threshold
steps.sub: 80+ block where safe · 50-79 alert · <50 context only

loop.label: new sighting or report: re-grade and reset age

C08-M06-L02-F2.note: Only the final, aged score decides what an indicator may do; an expired indicator is context only whatever its grade.
